content.text: hx of travel to areas where sanitation = poor
: crosses intestinal epithelium barrier thru M cells overlying the lymphoid follicles of Peyer’s patches
•may colonize the GB in chronic carriers
(faint pink or salmon-colored macular rash from trunk to extremities)
•onset 8-72hrs after exposure; generally self-limited (fever resolves 48-72hrs, diarrhea 4-10d; chart: 4-7d)
: sepsis risk in young, elderly & immunocompromised
Nonmotile facultative anaerobes; enterotoxins (ex, Shiga toxin)
: preferred dx test (identifies species); sensitivity testing to guide abx (resistance widespread)
▪︎antimotility drugs prolong illness: ⍉ in children w/ shigellosis & adults w/ bloody diarrhea
▪︎abx for symptomatic adults ⇢ shortens illness & bacterial shedding; most clear spontaneously
▪︎empiric: FQ, azithro, or 3rd-gen ceph (cefixime, ceftriaxone); adjust to susceptibility
▪︎children: ⍉FQs; azithro 1st-line. Mild dz + ⍉daycare ⇢ no tx needed
: hand washing; avoid sex, public swimming & food prep for others; continue several wks after diarrhea resolves (aSx shedding)
